schema.description: Run a JavaScript script that orchestrates step subagents deterministically, as a background task: the call returns at once and the run answers to workflow:<name>; its return value comes back through task_wait or on its own, starting a new turn if the conversation is idle. Below full access every call, resumes included, needs one user approval first. Runs outlive the turn, and a run interrupted by the app exiting resumes on its own when the conversation next runs. Completed steps are journaled, so resume_run_id replays them when you rerun a failed or stopped run.

args.description: Exposed to the script as `args`. Pass arrays and objects as JSON, not encoded strings; at most 4,096 items per array.

name.description: The run's id, address and task title, in the same namespace as agent names and reserved across this conversation's branch tree. A taken name is numbered (review-sweep-2) and the receipt reports the id it got; a resume needs an unused name and is not numbered.

resume_run_id.description: Id of an earlier run: its name, or the numbered id its receipt reported. Steps replay from the journal while every agent() call matches the last attempt in order (prompt and options except label and phase); a step left running when the run stopped re-runs alone; from the first changed, failed or skipped step on, everything re-runs. script and args default to the ones the run last used; an edited script changes later steps while unchanged ones still replay.

script.description:
Plain JavaScript (not TypeScript), starting with `export const meta = { name, description, phases?: [{title, detail?}] }` as a pure literal. The body runs as an async function (top-level await and return); its return value, JSON-serialized, is the workflow result, and steps still running when it returns are cancelled.
Globals:
- agent(prompt, opts?) -> Promise<any>: run one step subagent; it gets no conversation history, only the prompt. opts: label, phase (defaults to the latest phase() call), schema (JSON Schema; the promise then resolves to validated data instead of the step's final text), effort (low|medium|high|extra|max), agentType (a configured role name; the roles could not be read for this request, so none is listed, and a name is checked when its step starts: one that does not resolve fails the step to null), isolation. A failed or skipped step resolves to null.
- isolation: "worktree" gives the step its own git worktree of HEAD on a fresh branch (committed tree only, none of your uncommitted changes); kept if the step changed or committed anything, otherwise removed; its path and branch are shown to the user, not returned to the script. Needs the workspace to be a git repository root, else the step fails. Costs a full checkout per step.
- parallel(thunks) -> Promise<any[]>: start () => agent(...) thunks concurrently and wait for all (a barrier); a throwing thunk yields null.
- pipeline(items, ...stages) -> Promise<any[]>: each item flows through the stages on its own, with no barrier between stages; stages receive (prev, originalItem, index); a throwing stage makes that item null.
- phase(title): start a progress group (meta.phases fixes their order). log(message): one narration line on the progress card.
- args: the args input, verbatim; not defined when none was passed. budget: { total, spent(), remaining() } for token_budget; once exhausted, agent() throws.
Objects from args and step results have a null prototype: use JSON.stringify, not String() or template literals (log(obj) throws). Date.now(), argless new Date() and Math.random() throw (they would break resume replay); pass timestamps and seeds in args. No console, filesystem, network, module or timer access. Limits: 1000 agent() calls per run, 4096 items per array crossing the script boundary.
Required on a fresh run; optional with resume_run_id (the run's last script is reused).

token_budget.description: Token cap for the run's steps (budget.total). It is checked at each agent() call against tokens used by steps already finished, so running steps can overshoot it; not carried over on resume.
